title:
Your tenant is a $200 company.
*Who pays when rent stops?*

lines.say: You own a landed home. A company offers you 7,500 dollars a month on a two year lease. A corporate tenant feels safe.
lines.cap: a company offers *$7,500 a month* for 2 years

lines.say: They pay half the deposit and the first month's rent. After that, nothing. The family living there doesn't move out.
lines.cap: half the deposit, one month's rent. *then nothing*

lines.say: This happened in Kembangan this year. The owners are a couple in their 80s, and they had to go to court to get their house back.
lines.cap: the owners, in their 80s, *had to go to court*

lines.say: In October the court ruled for them. Repossession, double rent until they leave, and more than 55,000 dollars in arrears and costs.
The catch is that the company had only 200 dollars in paid up capital. Winning in court and actually getting paid are two very different things.
lines.cap: the company had *$200 in capital*. winning isn't getting paid

lines.say: Court reports show the same pattern at two other landed homes nearby, in 2019 and 2024.
lines.cap: the same pattern at *two other landed homes*

lines.say: What we've found protects landlords. Check the company's ACRA profile before you sign, ask the director for a personal guarantee, and collect the full deposit before you hand over the keys.
lines.cap: check *ACRA*, get a *personal guarantee*, collect the *full deposit*

lines.say: Leasing out your home soon? Comment tenant, and we'll send you our landlord checklist.

caption:
A company rented a landed home for $7,500 a month. Then the rent stopped. 🏠

In Kembangan this year, the owners, a couple in their 80s, had to go to court. In October the court ruled for them: repossession, double rent and more than $55,000 in arrears and costs. But the company had only $200 in paid up capital, and winning isn't the same as getting paid.

Before you sign: check the company's ACRA profile, ask the director for a personal guarantee, and collect the full deposit.

Leasing out your home soon? Comment TENANT for our landlord checklist 👇
